title: mitmdump flow printing is the Dumper addon (response/error hooks, echo_flow)
answers: How does mitmdump decide what to print for a flow?
How are errored flows printed in mitmdump?
body:
mitmdump has no direct printing; addons/dumper.py:Dumper is an ordinary addon.
- Hooks: response, error, websocket_message/end, tcp_message/error, udp_message/error, dns_response/error. No `request` hook, so an HTTP flow prints once on completion (response, or error if it failed first).
- Gate: Dumper.match -> False if flow_detail==0; else True if no filter or flowfilter.match(self.filter, f).
- Dumper.response and Dumper.error both call echo_flow: prints _echo_request_line if f.request (headers at flow_detail>=2, body via _echo_message at >=3, trailers >=2); _echo_response_line if f.response (2xx green, 3xx magenta, 4xx-5xx red, reason+size or '(content missing)'); if f.error prints ' << msg' bold red via strutils.escape_control_characters.
- So an errored flow prints request line, response line only if a response arrived, then the error. Response-then-error prints all three.
- tcp_error/udp_error use _proto_error: 'Error in TCP/UDP connection to <addr>: <error>' in red, subject to match. dns_error has its own handler (~line 418, not read).
